cues: Emily Dickinson lived almost her entire life in one house in Amherst, Massachusetts.
In later years she rarely went out, wore white, and spoke to some visitors from behind a door.
She wrote about eighteen hundred poems and published perhaps ten.
The rest she sewed into little booklets, which her sister found after her death.
The first selection was printed in eighteen ninety.
